title: Roman Britain (KS2)
subject: History
strapline: What the Romans did in Britain and what they left behind.
facts: The Romans came from Rome in Italy and built a huge empire across Europe.
Emperor Claudius led the successful Roman invasion of Britain in AD 43.
Queen Boudica of the Iceni led a revolt against the Romans around AD 60–61.
The Romans built straight roads, towns, forts, public baths and central heating (hypocausts).
Emperor Hadrian ordered a wall (Hadrian's Wall) built across northern Britain to mark and defend the frontier.
Latin was the Roman language; some English words and place-name endings (like -chester) come from it.
The Romans left Britain around AD 410 as their empire came under attack.

quick_quiz.q: In what year did the Romans successfully invade Britain?
Who led a British revolt against the Romans?
What wall marked the northern frontier of Roman Britain?

teacher_tips: Use a timeline BC/AD so children place the Romans among other periods.
Explore local Roman evidence (roads, place names) to make it real.
Discuss viewpoint: invasion looked very different to Romans and Britons.
